why: This is the textbook LRU cache: a hash map from key to node gives O(1) lookup, and a doubly linked list ordered by recency gives O(1) 'move to front' and 'evict from back'. The query-result story adds nothing beyond the serialised operation list.
hints: You need two O(1) operations: find a key, and find the least recently used key. No single structure does both.

Combine a dict key -> node with a doubly linked list ordered from most to least recent. get moves the node to the front; put inserts or updates at the front and, if over capacity, removes the node before the tail sentinel and deletes its key from the dict.
Use head/tail sentinel nodes so insert and unlink never special-case an empty list. O(1) per operation, O(capacity) space. (OrderedDict with move_to_end/popitem(last=False) is the same idea.)
pitfalls: A successful get must refresh the key's recency; a miss must not change anything.
Updating an existing key refreshes its recency but does not evict anything.
Return the string 'null' for each put and the value as a string for each get.
constraints:
• Not stated in the source; reasonable bounds for practice:
  • 1 <= capacity <= 3000
  • 1 <= operations.length <= 2 * 10^5
  • 0 <= key <= 10^4, 0 <= value <= 10^5
